evals.prompt: I just finished implementing the login feature. It touches auth.ts, login-form.tsx, styles.css, and I also fixed a typo in the README. Commit it all.
evals.expected_output: The skill should NOT commit everything together. It should split: (a) feat: login form component, (b) feat: auth API endpoint, (c) chore: fix typo in README — three separate atomic commits with descriptive messages.
expectations: Splits the work into logical atomic commits, not one bulk commit
Each commit message follows the type: description format
README typo fix is separated as chore/docs, not mixed with feature work

evals.prompt: I need to fix a critical production bug but I have half-finished work on my branch. What do I do?
evals.expected_output: Commit or stash the current work, create a fix branch from the last known-good commit on main, apply the hotfix, merge, then return to the feature branch.
expectations: Recommends stashing or committing in-progress work first
Creates a fix branch from main or the last stable commit
Does not suggest mixing the hotfix into the feature branch

evals.prompt: Our main branch has a bug that was introduced sometime in the last 30 commits. How do I find which commit caused it?
evals.expected_output: Use git bisect: mark current HEAD as bad, a known-good commit as good, and let git narrow down the offending commit by testing each midpoint.
expectations: Recommends git bisect with the correct workflow
Explains how to mark bad/good commits
Suggests a script or manual test at each bisect step

evals.prompt: Release v2.0.0: we added a breaking API change (removed deprecated endpoints) and fixed 3 bugs since v1.9.0. What version and what changelog entry?
evals.expected_output: Version 2.0.0 (breaking change = major bump). Changelog with Added/Changed/Fixed sections, a migration note for the removed endpoints, and a deprecation window reference.
expectations: Changelog has a migration note for the breaking change
Separates breaking changes from bug fixes in the changelog structure

evals.prompt: I need two agents to work on different features in the same repo at the same time without stepping on each other.
evals.expected_output: Use git worktrees: create separate worktree directories for each feature branch. Each agent works in isolation. Merge sequentially.
expectations: Recommends git worktrees, not just separate branches in the same working tree
Notes that changes remain isolated until explicitly merged
